newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Mandela opens talks with Zaire's Kabila in S.Africa.
newsitem.headline: Mandela opens talks with Zaire's Kabila in S.Africa.

text.p: South African President Nelson Mandela began talks with Zairean rebel leader Laurent Kabila in Cape Town on Wednesday evening to explore peace initiatives for the vast central African country.
The two leaders met at Mandela's official residence and shook hands briefly on the steps before walking back inside for talks behind closed doors.

The two leaders did not comment on the pending discussions but a senior government source told Reuters that Mandela hoped to arrange a direct meeting in South Africa between Kabila and ailing Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko.
Kabila left Zaire's Lubumbashi Airport for South Africa earlier in the day.
No definite arrangement had been made for a meeting between the two rivals, but the source predicted it could take place by the weekend.
In Kinshasa, Zaire's Information Minister Kin-Kiey Mulumba said President Mobutu Sese Seko and Kabila could meet shortly after negotiations between their envoys.
